newsitem.title: UK: SmithKline suspends arthritis treatment trial.
newsitem.headline: SmithKline suspends arthritis treatment trial.

text.p: Britain's SmithKline Beecham Plc said on Tuesday it had suspended Phase III tests of its IDEC-CE9.1/SB-210396 treatment for rheumatoid arthritis.

In a joint statement with U.S. group IDEC Pharmaceuticals Corp, SmithKline said the decision was based on observations of lowered CD4 cell courts in a higher number of treated patients in the Phase III study compared to the Phase II trial.
CD4 cells are key components of the immune system. Also known as "helper" T-cells, their number is a key signaller of immune status.

"While there have been no reports of side effects related to lower CD4 counts in this trial, the companies have decided to place a hold on the current clinical trials pending a thorough review and analysis of the data," they said in a statement.
The drug, also known as Primatized, caused "clinically significant improvement" in arthritis symptoms in Phase II trials, the companies reported in October.

The two companies said they "remained committed" to anti-CD4 approaches to treating rheumatoid arthritis and other auto-immune disease -- in which the body's immune system, for unknown reasons, turns on itself.
"In addition to the IDEC-CE9.1 antibody, a second-generation anti-CD4 antibody, IDEC-151/SB-217969, is currently in a Phase IIa trial for rheumatoid arthritis," the statement added.

"At high doses, this second-generation antibody did not lower CD4 cell counts for more than twenty-four hours in clinical trials to date and has demonstrated prolonged cell coating which may be important in both clinical activity and reduction in dosing frequency."
Shares in SmithKline Beecham fell 11-1/2p to 10.56 stg shortly after the announcement. In the United States NASDAQ halted trade on IDEC.
